messages:
alex-k: Heads up: scheduling a graceful cordon + rolling reboot across az21 next Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. Targeting 20 GPU nodes (cohort B) for NIC firmware + CUDA micropatch. Expect brief perf drops during drain + one 10–15m reboot per node. Please ack and flag any critical long-running jobs you know about.

maria-s: Ack. Which pools will be drained first? any tenant impact SLA to call out?

alex-k: We'll drain priority pools in this order: batch-low, batch-medium, realtime-narrow. Dedicated tenant pools (reserved) are NOT in scope unless we need manual migration. Expected capacity hit ~12-18% unless we backfill.
jin-ops: Proposed backfill plan: open a burst backfill window on saturn pool, allow preemptible containers to fill freed slots for up to 3 hours. After each node reboot we run a KV cache seed to avoid cold-start token spikes.

samir: Cost question — if we spin up burst on-demand GPUs in us-west for backfill that could add $$$. Can we instead shift noncritical jobs to existing spot pools first?
jin-ops: yes, plan is: 1) shift noncritical -> spot-pools (auto), 2) if slack persists, provision 4 temporary burst instances in az21-equivalent zone (short-lived). Budget cap set to $600 for the window.

maria-s: There's a customer long-run eval (cust-42) with pinned model running ramp test, started today and will hit 48h mark Tues 03:00 UTC — we should avoid evicting it. Can we add a keep label?

alex-k: Good catch. maria-s add label keep:during-maint to the job and I'll add an explicit exclusion to the drain script.
maria-s: done. label added.

ops-bot: Automated note: maintenance-ticket #INF-998 created. Rolling reboot script will run with concurrency=2. Estimated node reboot time 12-18m.

jin-ops: Drain command snippet we'll run (example):
```
kubectl cordon node-{{NODE}}
kubectl drain node-{{NODE}} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
# run reboot, then wait for Ready
```

samir: What observability should we watch? CPU/gpu-util, io-latency, and queue-depth on egress. Also watch prefix-cache hitrate to detect cold-token regen.
jin-ops: We'll hook a lightweight dashboard: per-pool token latency, prefix-cache hit rate, and reconnects. Alerts: >3x baseline token latency for 5m -> auto rollback trigger.

alex-k: Ops oncall, please coordinate customer comms for cust-42 and schedule a 1hr pre-maint check-in 01:00 UTC. Also, plan for a manual rollback if we see queue length spike >2x for >10m.

jin-ops: Acknowledged. I'll post runbook link + canary checklist in the #incidents channel 24h before.

maria-s: :thumbsup: thanks.

samir: small ask — can we set cache-seed burst after each reboot to warm KV for the most common prefixes? saves token-cost spikes.
jin-ops: Agreed, added to runbook. We'll run `redis-migrate --seed-prefixes recent-top-1000` after node-ready.

alex-k: Thanks team. If no objections I’ll ship comms to oncall and ops-bot will start automated reminders 48h -> 24h -> 1h.

maria-s: No objections from product.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: 48h before -> 24h before -> 1h before.
